title: hk pre-commit truncates files over 64 KiB through Oxfmt's stdin mode
description: Under 'bun run --bun', 'oxfmt --stdin-filepath X < X' writes at most 65536 bytes of output (reproduced: a 1,020,982-byte THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md came back as 65,536 bytes). hk's oxfmt step uses that stdin mode for check_diff, so a pre-commit on any formatted file larger than 64 KiB commits it truncated; this happened to THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md during proposal 0002. 0002 excludes that generated file from oxfmt in hk.pkl and .oxfmtrc.jsonc. Every other file stays exposed. Expected: the hook never shortens a file; find whether Bun's stdout flushing on exit or oxfmt is at fault, and fix the step (e.g. drop check_diff or run oxfmt through a path that flushes).

title: Processes a bash command leaves behind outlive pico
description: Found while implementing proposal 0008 (PR #45). OMP's embedded shell keeps a command's & child running after the command returns (it retains the shell so such processes survive across turns), and OMP lists a job's processes only while its run is in flight. Neither engine dispose nor pico's exit kills such a process. Observed 2026-11-02: (1) a foreground bash call '/bin/sleep 127 & echo started': after createPicoSession + prompt + dispose, the sleep was reparented to init and still running; (2) a background job '/bin/sh -c ... & ' that completed: its child survived stop, dispose and the process exit (adversarial re-review of acdd22a); (3) a job that forks + setsid (daemonizes) escapes both pid and process-group tracking. Proposal 0008 stops running jobs and jobs the model killed, which OMP lists reliably; tracking event-sampled pids for leftovers proved unreliable and was removed. Expected (proposal 0008 quality bar, proposal 0001 / PROTOTYPE 'no orphaned execution'): nothing the agent started survives session disposal or pico's exit. Likely needs a different mechanism (e.g. Pico-owned process-group/session or OMP support).

title: Connect the Mac app's Models pane and settings file row to pico settings
description: Follow-up to proposal 0007 (PR #46), split out by Mark on 2026-11-02 as a PR they expect to need no proposal: connect the Mac app's Models pane and General > Settings file row to Pico settings through the `pico settings get`, `pico models list` and `pico settings update` commands 0007 specifies, and remove the app's sample-data mode. Decisions Mark already made for it: the app reads and writes settings only through `pico`; a model must be chosen (no 'Oh My Pi Default' picker entry, 'Not Set' until one is saved); sample data is removed rather than kept beside real values. The design below was drafted in 0007 before the split; the remaining open details (how the app finds `pico`, the pane states, the notice wording) need Mark's confirmation when the PR starts. Completes prototype criterion 15's app half.
design:
### The Mac app

#### Finding and running `pico`

- The app runs the executable named by the `-PicoExecutable <path>` launch argument when one is given, reading the argument domain only, never saved defaults. Otherwise it runs the first executable file of `/opt/homebrew/bin/pico` and `/usr/local/bin/pico`. `mise run macos:run` builds `.build/pico` with `pico:build` and opens the app with `-PicoExecutable` set to it.
- When no executable is found, the app runs nothing. The Models pane says `pico` was not found at those locations and that Homebrew installs it.
- The app runs `pico` off the main thread, with no stdin and the app's own environment. A run that has not finished within 30 seconds is terminated and reported as "`pico` did not answer within 30 seconds".
- On exit status 0 the app decodes stdout. Otherwise it decodes the last line of stderr as an error document and shows its `message`. Failing that, it shows the last lines of stderr, or the exit status when stderr is empty. A document whose `apiVersion` is not 1 is reported as this `pico` speaking a different version, naming its path.
- The app loads by running `pico settings get` and `pico models list` concurrently, when its window opens and each time the Models pane is shown.
- To save, it runs `pico settings update --default-model <value> --if-revision <revision>` when a model is chosen, or `--default-thinking <value> --if-revision <revision>` when a level is chosen, with the revision from its last load. `pico` decides the level a new model keeps. A successful receipt updates the shown values and revision.
- On `CONFLICT`, the app reloads and shows an alert saying that Pico's settings changed outside the window, nothing was saved, and the current values are shown. Any other failure shows an alert with its message, and the pickers keep the last loaded values.

#### Models

- **Loading:** both pickers are disabled and read "Loading…".
- **Command failure:** both pickers are disabled and read "Unavailable". The Defaults footer shows the failure with a Try Again button that loads again.
- **Unsupported or invalid settings file:** both pickers are disabled and read "Unavailable". The footer shows the problem, says to fix or remove the file, and has a Show in Finder button that reveals it.
- **Loaded, file missing or valid:**
    - The Model picker lists the catalog. Each entry shows the model's name and then its provider in parentheses, such as "Claude Sonnet 5.5 (anthropic)", because two providers can offer models with the same name.
    - With no saved default, the Model picker reads "Not Set", and the Reasoning level picker is disabled and reads "Not Set". "Not Set" cannot be chosen once a model is saved. When `effective` names a built-in choice, the footer says that until a model is chosen, new sessions start with that model.
    - A saved model that is not in the catalog appears as its saved value followed by "(unavailable)", selected. The footer says new sessions will fail to start until another model is chosen.
    - The Reasoning level picker lists the saved model's thinking choices and shows the saved level.
    - Choosing a model or level saves it at once. While a save runs, both pickers are disabled.
    - With an empty catalog, the Model picker is disabled and reads "None available", and the footer says no model has usable credentials.
    - The Defaults footer otherwise says that new Sesh sessions start with this model and reasoning level, and that sessions already open, or given a model in Sesh, keep their own.
- **Available models** lists the catalog in order. Each row shows the model's name and its `provider/id` value, with "Default" on the saved model. An empty catalog reads "None available". While loading or after a failure, the section reads "Unavailable".
- The Models pane shows no notice about unconnected settings, because it has none.

#### General › Settings file

- The row shows `settingsFile` from the last load on one line, truncated in the middle if it does not fit. Before a load it reads "Loading…", and after a failure it reads "Unavailable".
- Show in Finder reveals the file selected when it exists. When only its folder exists, it opens the folder. Otherwise it is disabled. Copy Path, in the row's context menu, copies the path whenever one is shown.
- The Runtime and Versions rows stay unconnected.

#### Removing sample data

- Delete the sample-data mode, including:
    - `app/Sample/` and its tests;
    - the View › Show Sample Data command, the `-ShowsSampleData` argument and the sample-data notice;
    - the provider list rows, provider pages, the Add Provider sheet, the sign-in menu and Sign Out;
    - the sample Register and Unregister actions;
    - provider tiles, and the provider logo assets with their notice, `app/ThirdPartyNotices.md`.
- Navigation no longer has provider pages, and the history rule for forgetting them goes too.
- Every unconnected row keeps its unconnected stub. Providers & Accounts shows its Providers row reading "Not connected" and a disabled Add Provider… button.
- The notice at the bottom of every pane except Models reads "Some settings aren't connected yet". It keeps the symbol and accessibility announcement of today's unconnected notice.
- Search, links and item slugs are unchanged.

title: Formatter hook reports ignored generated files as failures
description: During proposal.0003 verification, editing the ignored generated .build/pico-acp launcher for the user-authorized temporary Sesh preview triggered format-after-edit. The hook calls mise run fmt for every changed regular project file without filtering ignored/unsupported inputs (.omp/extensions/format-after-edit.ts:10-20,37-56). Oxfmt exited 2 with Expected at least one target file; all matched files may have been excluded by ignore rules. The same happened when integrating generated .beads/issues.jsonl rows. Expected: intentionally ignored/generated targets are skipped without a false formatter failure, while real parse/format failures remain visible. Repro: edit one line in the generated ignored .build/pico-acp through the agent edit tool. Do not rerun destructive cleanup. Outside proposal.0003 because it affects development-harness formatting, not Pico's runtime delegation boundary. First step: scope the hook's candidate files to supported, non-ignored formatter inputs; add behavioral coverage for an all-ignored edit batch.
notes:
Also reproduced while implementing proposal.0005 in issue-18 worktree: every new app/**/*.swift and app/Localizable.xcstrings write triggers mise run fmt/Oxfmt, which exits 2 because it does not support those file types. Native sources are formatted by macos:fmt instead. This is the same unsupported-input filter defect, not Swift parse evidence; leave hook repair outside the app UI scope.
Related manifestation observed during proposal0004/PR40 (pico-rrn): editing one line in prepared node_modules/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent/src/sdk.ts through edit caused the lifecycle hook to run the project's formatter on the vendored file, reformatting the whole SDK source from5773 to6420 lines. The hook passes every edited regular project path without ignore/vendor filtering (format-after-edit.ts:10-15,51-55). Bun patch preparation kept the package cache safe; exact package contents were restored with mise run deps:install -- --force --ignore-scripts and the committed minimal patch. A future hook fix should skip git-ignored/vendor ownership as well as unsupported generated inputs, preserving narrowly scoped dependency patches. Deferred here: harness behavior, not adapter session persistence.
